newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM sees Oct pulp price hike to $620-630.
newsitem.headline: UPM sees Oct pulp price hike to $620-630.

text.p: Juha Niemela, chief executive of UPM-Kymmene Oy, Europe's largest forest industry group, said on Wednesday an announced rise in the market price of pulp to $620-630 per tonne from $580 seemed realistic.
"Announcements have been sent to clients of price hikes to $620-630 in October," Niemela told a seminar. Just a few weeks ago, such price hikes would have seemed unrealistic, he said.
"However, in the past few days, information of stoppages at mills in the United States and Canada suggests that these (new prices) can be regarded as realistic," Niemela said.
Speaking in broad terms about the forest industry, Niemela did not make it clear which companies had announced the pulp price hikes nor did he specify whether UPM-Kymmene was among them.

Due to seasonal factors, a rise of "a few hundred thousand tonnes" in August in the so called NorScan pulp inventory (North American and Scandinavian pulp stocks) would "not be alarming," he said. In July, NorScan pulp stocks rose to some 1.7 million tonnes from about 1.5 million in June.
August NorScan figures have not yet been published.
